newsitem.title: CHILE: Peru, Ecuador meet for peace talks in Chile.
newsitem.headline: Peru, Ecuador meet for peace talks in Chile.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Peru and Ecuador met in Chile on Monday for two days of talks aimed at resolving their Amazon border dispute, Chilean officials said.
Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza, host of the talks, said they would focus on the delicate issue of how and where to demarcate the border.

"The famous problem with border demarcation is the main issue, but it's not our place to comment on that," he told reporters after meeting foreign ministers Francisco Tudela of Peru and Galo Leoro of Ecuador.
"The climate is good, there's going to some progress and I hope the parties make an effort to solve problems," he said.
The goal is to iron out terms for wider-ranging talks in Brazil on the border dispute, Chilean officials said. The date of the Brazil talks will depend on progress made here, they said.

Chile, Brazil, Argentina and the United States are guarantors of a 1942 border treaty between Peru and Ecuador. Ecuador later renounced the treaty, alleging it was signed under pressure, and the dispute flared into war last January.
